execution_steps: 1. Continuing the FF6 mission per event 270's exact_next_action -- applying the 'is the official data actually embedded in the pinned spec cache' check (proven 4 times this session for xliff's module/core schemas) to UBL's blocked code-list obligations, which had previously assumed 'no verified spec source for either the list content or the genericode distribution schema.'

2. Grepped .local/format-contracts/acquired/ubl/*.bin for genericode/UNCL/ISO4217/ISO3166 references, finding 9 mentions of 'genericode' in src-ubl-001.bin (descriptive prose only) but noticed src-ubl-002.bin was suspiciously massive (261,521 lines as a text dump vs 7,308 for src-ubl-001.bin).

3. Read the first bytes of src-ubl-002.bin directly and found a 'PK' zip magic-number header -- confirmed via Python's zipfile module that it opens as a valid ZIP with 927 entries, including a cl/gc/default/ directory containing 16 genuine OASIS genericode (.gc) files (CurrencyCode, CountryIdentificationCode, UnitOfMeasureCode, and 13 others).

4. Read one file's content directly (CurrencyCode-2.3.gc) and confirmed it is the authentic, complete ISO 4217 currency code list in OASIS genericode 1.0 XML format, with real values (AED, AFN, ALL, ...), not a summary or placeholder.

5. Extracted 11 of the 16 files (excluding the '-incl-deprecated'/'-incl-deleted' superset variants, keeping current/non-deprecated values only) to src/format_factory/ubl/model/codelists/ -- 4.87MB combined uncompressed.

6. Wrote genericode.py's parse_genericode(), first attempting namespace-qualified lookups for every element per the genericode namespace declaration, then discovering by direct ElementTree inspection that ONLY the document's own root element carries the gc: prefix in these real files -- every descendant (Identification, ColumnSet, Row, Value, ...) is unprefixed/no-namespace. Corrected the parser to match the actual file structure rather than the schema's informal description.

7. Designed the parser to read the document's own declared ColumnSet/Key/ColumnRef to find the primary identifying column, rather than hardcoding 'code' as a column name -- verified all 11 real files happen to use 'code', then wrote a dedicated test with a differently-named key column to prove the parser doesn't assume the convention.

8. Wired official_code_list_registry() composing load_bundled_code_lists() with the already-existing CodeListRegistry.register(), with zero special-casing, matching codelist.py's own 'official and custom register identically' design exactly.

9. Hit a real constraint on first test run: this package's own security-baseline test forbids importing 'importlib' anywhere in src/ (a supply-chain hardening rule). Initially used importlib.resources for package-data access; switched to plain pathlib.Path(__file__).parent, matching the exact pattern the xliff package's own bundled-schema loader (built earlier this session) already uses.
10. Ran the pre-existing ubl suite (987 passed) BEFORE writing any new test, confirming zero regressions from the wiring alone.

11. Probed interactively: all 11 lists load with plausible real counts (179 currencies, 498 countries, 1732 units); USD/EUR/GBP are members of CurrencyCode; US/DE are members of CountryIdentificationCode; KGM/MTR are members of UnitOfMeasureCode; end-to-end validate_code() against a real Code object correctly reports valid/invalid.

12. Added a package-data entry to pyproject.toml, built a real wheel via `pip wheel .`, and confirmed all 11 .gc files ship inside it byte-identical to source (spot-checked CurrencyCode-2.3.gc) before writing any dependent code.

13. Wrote 14 new tests, updated codelist.py's own module docstring (which explicitly claimed the data/loader combination was unavailable) and the sibling test file's stale docstring to point at genericode.py instead.
14. Ran the full ubl suite (987 -> 1001 passed), ruff, and mypy --strict on the full ubl source tree (35 files) -- all clean.
15. Ran the combined 6-format regression suite (3538 -> 3552 passed, same 4 pre-existing unrelated safetensors interop failures, 2 skipped) -- zero regression beyond the 14 new tests.

16. Updated both obligations' evidence: PROMOTED partial->implemented (both the loading mechanism AND the officially-sourced data now genuinely exist, fully resolving the compound gap), added the 14 new tests to positive/negative selectors, added UBL-OFFICIAL-CODE-LISTS-GENERICODE-LOADER-PROOF to execution_evidence_ids.
